global.criterion: Coherent dimensional 3D illustration with believable materials, geometry, depth and contact shadows, not flat line art.
No readable or invented text, letters, numerals, arrows, logos, watermarks or pseudo-writing anywhere.
No real or rendered people, faces, hands, visible helpers or presenter characters. Clearly synthetic faceless training mannequins are permitted only if the asset asks for one.
No real injury, exposed wound, active chemical spill, actual emergency action or treatment on a real person; the scene is clearly a training simulation.

s102-video-assess.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: first-person eye-level scan at field access gate; no body visible. A camera-view safety scan pauses behind a simple barrier before a simulated field incident. Show a separate vehicle route, uneven ground and a distant blank training mannequin; no person, face, helper or character is visible.

s102-video-alert.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: first-person close view of a safe mock call area; no hands visible. A blank phone screen and blank site card lie on a clean station inside the safe zone. A clearly open access path is visible beyond a barrier; no person, character, hands or actual call is shown.
blank phone and card for overlays

s102-video-injury.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: low three-quarter view of a faceless training mannequin. A clearly synthetic mannequin rests in a safe field shelter with its ankle untouched in the found position. Clean unused gauze and gloves are nearby as teaching props. No person, helper, blood or real wound appears.
limb left in its found position

s102-video-heat.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: single continuous shaded training tableau at eye level. A clearly synthetic faceless training mannequin sits under a field shade with cooling cloth and fan ready. Small moisture beads on the mannequin show that sweating can coexist with a possible severe heat-illness scenario; a blank phone prop indicates a simulated call. No person, character, medication or drink appears.

s102-video-chemical.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: side tracking view of an empty training wash route. A clear route leads from an unopened neutral training bottle to a maintained full eyewash station. Use only unused props and no person, hands, real chemical discharge or eye washing. The bottle has no label or pictogram.

s102-video-kit.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: first-person eye-level kit display at a field shelter; no hands visible. An open clean training first-aid kit displays unused gauze, gloves, blanket and blank contact card; a full eyewash station is separately visible in the background. The small eye-rinse bottle is a starter prop, not the sole provision. No person or character appears.

s102-video-road-case.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: diagonal eye-level view along the vehicle route. A clearly synthetic mannequin represents a simulated fall well away from a stationary vehicle route. Barrier and open access path show the safe approach; no person, helper or character is visible, and the mannequin is not pulled upright.

s102-video-dizzy-case.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: medium close view of a remote shade-shelter training tableau. A faceless synthetic torso mannequin sits beneath shade beside a fan, damp cooling cloth and blank mock-call phone. Moisture beads indicate that sweating is possible; no visible person, helper, diagnosis label or oral drink appears.

s102-video-ankle-case.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: side view of shallow hidden-hole training zone. A visibly synthetic full mannequin remains in its found position beside a shallow concealed-hole prop. An emergency call card and safe access route are visible but no person, character, hands, pulling or limb straightening occurs.

s102-video-eye-case.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: eye-level route toward a full eyewash station. An unopened neutral training bottle on a table stands near a clear route to a full eyewash station. No chemical discharge, exposed eye, person, helper or hands appears; a blank space remains for the editable action sequence overlay.

s102-video-kit-case.criterion: Scene composition matches this camera and task: close three-quarter view of kit shelf and wash route. Clean gauze and a blank contact card are placed outside an open training kit beside a separate full eyewash station. Tweezers stay unused; no medicine, wound, person, character or hands appear. Blank surfaces remain available for editable overlays.

s1-02-scene-safety-still.criterion: Scene is this original still composition: wide high three-quarter spatial model from above-left. Field access junction as a compact 3D model: stationary training mannequin away from a visible traffic route, safe observation zone behind a barrier and empty upper-left margin for overlays. No person, character or eye-level rescue motion.
This is a static composition with the stated camera, not an eye-level action shot.

s1-02-heat-comparison-still.criterion: Scene is this original still composition: two separate parallel field-shelter prop vignettes seen from above. Left: alert scenario represented by a faceless synthetic mannequin seated in shade with unused cooling props; right: severe-warning scenario represented by a separate faceless synthetic mannequin with moisture beads and a blank call phone. Both may show moisture; no person, helper, diagnosis label or oral drink. Blank divider and margins for editable localized labels.
This is a static composition with the stated camera, not an eye-level action shot.

s1-02-aid-kit-still.criterion: Scene is this original still composition: close tabletop three-quarter inventory layout. Unused gauze, tape, blanket, small starter eye-rinse bottle and blank contact card on a clean table. A maintained full eyewash station sits visibly apart in the soft-focus background. No label, medicine name or injury.
This is a static composition with the stated camera, not an eye-level action shot.
